keyboard.behavior: Default shortcut=true toggles every enabled instance, even from editable controls. All live guide instances opt out to avoid colliding with documentation search.
Wraps through enabled visible commands, keeping input focus and updating aria-activedescendant.
Selects first/last enabled result, including when editing the search input; these keys do not move its text caret.
Selects the active result only when the search input is focused. Command selection is pointerdown, not click or automatic link navigation.
Requests hide and focus return; a hide listener can veto closing.

Wraps at the first/last focusable control. Options here are div nodes with tabindex=-1, leaving search and close as the boundary controls. Native buttons remain in the extension focusable query even with tabindex=-1; this is not a document focus guard.

guidelines: Import both optional CSS and the named CommandPalette extension. Do not import it from the core barrel or load two runtime graphs.
Use a hidden named div root, a labelled command-palette-input and a command-palette-list. The constructor adds dialog/combobox/listbox roles; it does not call showModal or make the background inert.

Set shortcut=false on all but a single intentional shortcut owner. The default does not ignore editable targets, key repeats or other palette instances. This guide preserves docs search as the closed-state Ctrl/Command+K owner.
Filtering trims and lowercases the query, matching the combined visible text and data-keywords by substring. It does not fold accents or tokenize words. Query text persists after closing.
All emitted CustomEvents bubble and are cancelable, but only show, hide and select read preventDefault. Payloads live in event.detail, unlike core direct event properties.

select is the veto gate; selected reports the accepted command. closeOnSelect requests hide before selected, but a canceled hide can leave the palette open. Neither event executes business actions automatically.
Initialize dynamic roots explicitly after insertion. Repeating initCommandPalette on the same scope does not rescan it; its descendant query does not include the supplied root itself.

dispose closes even when hide would be vetoed and removes instance listeners. Generated roles/IDs remain. This extension has no nested-overlay coordination, native top layer or global focus guard; evaluate those limitations before shipping.

sourceOptions.name: shortcut
sourceOptions.description: Global Ctrl/Meta+K toggle; false in every guide instance so docs search remains the owner.

sourceOptions.name: closeOnSelect
sourceOptions.description: Requests hide before selected; false keeps the palette open. A hide veto also leaves it open.

events.filter.trm.command-palette: detail = { query, results }; results counts enabled visible commands. Disabled matches still suppress the empty state.
events.hidden.trm.command-palette: After close cleanup. dispose closes without dispatching this lifecycle pair.
events.hide.trm.command-palette: Cancelable gate before hiding, overflow restoration and opener focus return.
events.select.trm.command-palette: Cancelable selection gate; detail = { command, value }, with value from data-value or trimmed text. Preventing it blocks the hide request and selected.
events.selected.trm.command-palette: Accepted selection, with the same detail payload, after the optional hide request. Canceling this notification does not undo selection.
events.show.trm.command-palette: Cancelable gate before exposing the root, locking root overflow and focusing search.
events.shown.trm.command-palette: After the immediate show setup and filter notification; not a CSS-transition completion promise.

guidelines: Forms is a composition of CSS/native controls, not a Forms class or plugin. Most partials use the forms layer; Input group uses components. Enhanced Chips, Combobox, Datepicker, OTP, Range and Strength have separate component APIs.
Use form-control for native selects, check and radio on the input, and a switch wrapper for switch styling. Retired form-select/form-check/form-switch aliases are not strict core.

Provide visible labels and real input types, name/value, autocomplete and constraints appropriate for your application. Placeholder text is a hint, not a label. These examples deliberately use no real account or password submission.

Use fieldset/legend for related choices. Disabled values are omitted; readonly is only for supported text-like controls, not select/checkbox/radio. Fieldset does not automatically disable links or custom widgets.
Keep floating labels before their controls. Associate meaningful input-group addons with aria-describedby rather than replacing the visible label or accessible name.

Visual feedback does not set aria-invalid, generate error text, focus a summary or validate a server request. The copied local demo owns those tasks. data-trm-validate opts into native user-invalid styles; success additionally needs its valid token.

The representative token table mixes root shared properties with component-local map entries. Root input/button sizing is reused selectively; local defaults can override inheritance. Consult individual form topics for their complete maps.

Native controls work without framework JavaScript. Demo submission/inspection buttons start disabled until the application handlers are installed; this safety setup is documentation code, not core behavior.

keyboard.behavior: Native controls and the explicitly focusable named scrolling regions enter the tab order. Table rows are not focusable grid items.
A focused overflowing wrapper can scroll through native browser behavior. No cell-navigation or sorting plugin is installed.

guidelines: Table styling is opt-in: use .table. Captions and scoped column/row headers remain the semantic foundation; this is not an ARIA grid.
Theme classes apply to a table, row or cell. The inset shadow accent cascade prefers state over stripe over theme/base colors; text and borders use corresponding theme tokens.
Direct-child selectors and reset accent variables keep nested table accents independent. Theme custom properties inherited from an ancestor are not magically erased.

table-responsive establishes an inline-size query container and horizontal scrolling. Prefixed responsive overflow is controlled by viewport media queries, whereas prefixed table-stacked rules use container queries; do not conflate them.
Use sm:, md:, lg:, xl: and 2xl: prefixes, not suffix-style table-responsive-md. Stacked tables require a query container and data-cell on td elements for visual labels.
Stacking changes CSS display but keeps real headers. Generated labels supplement rather than replace header associations; validate real screen readers for your data before release.
Name and focus overflow regions for keyboard access. Overflow clipping may hide menus/tooltips; do not promise those widgets can escape it.
Hover and active classes are visual accents, not row selection, sorting or fetching. Those features belong to application code, not a Table plugin.
